title: Good Debt and Harmful Debt
concept: Debt should be evaluated by its purpose, total cost, repayment terms, and whether the borrower can afford the repayments.
learningObjective: Understand that debt can be more or less useful depending on why the money is borrowed, how much it costs, and whether it can be repaid comfortably.
secondaryMisconceptions: Borrowing for education or a business is always a good decision.
A small monthly repayment means a loan is automatically affordable.
keyTakeaway: Debt is not automatically good or bad; purpose, cost, terms, and affordability matter.

screens.title: Same Loan, Different Result?
screens.content: Two people borrow money for useful reasons. One loan helps, while the other causes trouble. Is the purpose enough?
screens.illustration: Two borrowing cards show useful purchases. One path leads to a balanced budget, while the other leads to an overflowing repayment calendar.

screens.title: Four Borrowing Choices
screens.content: A family is comparing loans for education, a work tool, a luxury phone, and everyday expenses. Each choice has different costs and consequences.
screens.illustration: Four cards show a course, sewing machine, premium phone, and grocery basket.

screens.title: Purpose Is Only One Clue
screens.content: A useful purchase can still become difficult if fees are high or repayments leave too little for food, transport, and other needs.
screens.illustration: A useful course card sits beside a large fee tag and an essential-expense envelope with too little money.

screens.title: Sort With Care
screens.content: Your task is not to call every debt good or bad. Use the purpose, total cost, repayment plan, and family budget.
screens.illustration: Four magnifying glasses are labelled Purpose, Total Cost, Repayments, and Affordability.

screens.title: What Should You Check?
screens.question: What information matters most before deciding whether debt may be useful or risky?

options.text: Purpose, total cost, repayments, and affordability
options.response: Good thinking. A useful purpose is only part of the decision. The full cost and effect on essential spending also matter.

options.text: Whether the monthly repayment sounds small
options.response: A small payment may continue for many months. The total amount repaid could still be high.
An important-looking purchase can still have expensive or unaffordable loan terms.
Another person’s decision does not show whether the loan fits this borrower’s income and budget.

screens.title: Sort the Borrowing Decisions
screens.instruction: Place each borrowing decision under Potentially Useful, Risky, or Depends on Situation. Use all the details, not only the purchase.

educationalAssumptions: The examples involve adults or families making borrowing decisions.
A trusted adult reviews the loan details.
The stated repayments and total costs are simplified classroom examples.
A useful purchase does not guarantee future income or success.
Real loans may include different interest rates, fees, penalties, and repayment conditions.
The activity does not recommend taking any loan.

categories.label: Potentially Useful Debt
categories.description: Borrowing that may create lasting value, has manageable terms, and leaves enough money for essential needs.

categories.label: Risky Debt
categories.description: Borrowing that is difficult to afford, mainly pays for an optional purchase, or disrupts essential spending.

categories.label: Depends on Situation
categories.description: Borrowing that could help or harm depending on the loan cost, repayment plan, income, timing, and available alternatives.

sortableItems.title: Affordable Education Course
sortableItems.decision: Borrow £600 for a verified skills course that may improve future work opportunities.
details: Total repayment: £660
Repayment: £55 per month for 12 months
The family can cover the repayment without reducing food, transport, or emergency savings
The course may improve skills, but employment is not guaranteed
sortableItems.explanation: The course may create lasting value, the total cost is clear, and the repayments appear manageable in this scenario.

sortableItems.title: Tool for Paid Work
sortableItems.decision: Borrow £300 for a sewing machine needed to complete existing customer orders.
details: Total repayment: £336
Repayment: £28 per month for 12 months
The borrower already has confirmed orders
Repayments leave enough money for essential expenses
Future income is still not guaranteed
sortableItems.explanation: The tool may help generate income, and the repayment appears affordable. It remains important to recognise that earnings are never guaranteed.

sortableItems.title: Unaffordable Luxury Phone
sortableItems.decision: Borrow £900 for a premium phone even though the current phone still works.
details: Total repayment: £1,080
Repayment: £90 per month for 12 months
The repayment would reduce money available for food and transport
The purchase is an optional upgrade
sortableItems.explanation: The optional purchase costs more through borrowing and would make important expenses harder to cover.

sortableItems.title: Temporary Everyday Expenses
sortableItems.decision: Borrow £200 for groceries and transport during a one-month delay in family income.
details: Total repayment: £220
The delayed income is expected next month
The family has a repayment plan
It is unclear whether cheaper or safer alternatives are available
sortableItems.explanation: The borrowing covers essential needs and may solve a temporary problem. However, the cost, alternatives, and repayment certainty still need checking.

sortableItems.title: Expensive Education Loan
sortableItems.decision: Borrow £600 for an education course with very high charges.
details: Total repayment: £1,020
Repayment: £170 per month for six months
The repayment would reduce the grocery budget
The course may be useful, but its results are uncertain
sortableItems.explanation: Education may create value, but the high total cost and unaffordable repayments could make this loan harmful. The purpose alone does not decide the result.

contextDependentItems: Borrowing for education with high fees or unaffordable repayments
Borrowing for a business or work tool without clear demand or a manageable repayment plan
ambiguityExplanation: The same purchase can belong in different categories when the loan terms or family situation change.
An affordable education loan may be potentially useful.
An education loan with very high fees or repayments that reduce grocery money may be risky.
A work tool may help create income, but it is not automatically a good loan if no customers exist or repayments are unaffordable.
placementRules: Every item must be placed in one category.
Use the purpose, total repayment, repayment amount, and effect on essential needs.
Each item has one recommended category based on the details provided.
The category applies only to this scenario, not to every similar loan.
config.validationMethod: Check all five items after submission. Keep correct items in place and return incorrect items with a short explanation.
config.retryBehavior: Keep correctly sorted items in place. Return only incorrect items to the centre, provide one short hint, and allow unlimited retries.

accessibilityAlternative.method: Present each borrowing decision as a card with three buttons: Potentially Useful, Risky, and Depends on Situation.
accessibilityAlternative.screenReaderInstruction: Listen to the loan purpose, total cost, monthly repayment, and effect on essential spending. Then choose the most suitable category.

feedback.success: Excellent sorting. You checked more than the reason for borrowing—you also considered cost, repayment terms, and essential spending.
feedback.incorrect: Look beyond the purchase. Does the total repayment fit the budget without reducing money for essential needs?
feedback.incomplete: Sort all five borrowing decisions before checking your answer.

screens.title: Look Beyond Good and Bad
screens.content: You sorted debt using more than its purpose. Debt is money borrowed and repaid later, often with interest or fees. It may be useful when it creates lasting value and repayments are affordable. It may be harmful when costs are high or essential needs are squeezed. Education and business borrowing are not automatically good, and optional borrowing is not automatically manageable. Check the purpose, total repayment, loan length, income, and money left for essentials.
screens.simpleSummary: Judge debt by its purpose, full cost, and effect on the budget.
screens.illustration: A borrowing decision passes through four checkpoints labelled Purpose, Total Cost, Repayment Terms, and Affordable?

screens.title: The Bicycle Repair Loan
screens.content: A parent needs a bicycle for travelling to work. The repair costs £120. Before borrowing, the family checks the total repayment, monthly cost, other transport choices, and whether food money remains protected. The repair is useful, but the loan is sensible only if the terms are affordable.
screens.illustration: A bicycle repair card sits beside a repayment calendar, grocery envelope, and alternative bus route.

questions.text: Which borrowing decision appears potentially useful in the situation described?

options.text: A work tool with affordable repayments and confirmed orders
options.feedback: Correct. The tool may create lasting value, has a clear use, and leaves essential spending protected.

options.text: A luxury watch that reduces grocery money
options.feedback: The purchase is optional, and the repayment would make an essential expense harder to cover.

options.text: A new phone when the current phone works
options.feedback: An optional upgrade may not create enough lasting value to justify borrowing costs.

options.text: A loan with unknown fees and no repayment plan
options.feedback: Without the total cost and repayment plan, it is difficult to judge whether the borrowing is affordable.

questions.correctExplanation: The tool may create lasting value, there is a clear use for it, and the repayments leave essential spending protected.
questions.misconceptionTested: A debt’s purpose is the only information needed to judge it.

questions.text: Which statement about debt is most accurate?

options.text: Debt can be useful or harmful depending on its terms and affordability
options.feedback: Correct. Purpose, total cost, repayment period, income, and essential spending all matter.
Some borrowing may create lasting value and remain affordable, while other borrowing can cause financial pressure.
Education may be useful, but high fees or unaffordable repayments can still make the loan harmful.

options.text: A loan is affordable whenever the monthly payment is small
options.feedback: A small payment may continue for a long time and create a high total repayment.

questions.correctExplanation: The purpose matters, but the total cost, repayment period, income, and money remaining for essentials also affect the result.

questions.text: A tablet costs £500, but a loan asks for £15 monthly for 60 months. What should the borrower check first?

options.text: The £900 total repayment and whether it fits the budget
options.feedback: Correct. Sixty payments of £15 total £900, so the full cost and affordability matter.
The monthly amount is only one part of the loan. Sixty payments create a much larger total cost.
Excitement does not show whether the loan is affordable or good value.

options.text: Whether the first payment is affordable
options.feedback: The borrower must be able to manage the full repayment period, not only the first month.

questions.correctExplanation: Sixty payments of £15 total £900. The borrower must consider the full cost and whether all repayments leave enough for essential needs.
questions.misconceptionTested: A small monthly repayment means a loan is automatically affordable.

screens.message: You learned to check why money is borrowed, what it costs, and whether repayments fit the budget.

screens.instruction: Create two imaginary loans for the same £100 item. Give them different fees and repayment periods, then compare the total repayment. Do not borrow real money.

reviewChecklist.notes: The mission focuses on evaluating debt using purpose, cost, repayment terms, and affordability.
The loan examples distinguish the amount borrowed, total repayment, monthly repayments, fees, and impact on essential spending.
The learner evaluates simplified family borrowing decisions rather than being encouraged to take debt personally.
The mission does not discuss investing.
The mission states that education and work tools may create value but do not guarantee employment, customers, or income.
The mission does not discuss stocks or markets.
Borrowing is discussed neutrally, including situations where families may need help covering essential expenses.
The mission avoids calling all education or business borrowing good and explains how the same purpose can produce different results.
The mission uses pounds, education, everyday expenses, phones, work tools, groceries, and transport familiar to UK learners.
The learner sorts borrowing decisions using purpose, total cost, repayments, and effect on essential spending.
The quiz addresses the belief that all debt is harmful, education borrowing is always good, and small payments always mean affordability.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed in under five minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The mission uses three short story screens, five sorting cards, and three concise quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The wording is concrete, supportive, and suitable for children aged 8–12.
